'''''Nicandra ''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Solanaceae]], native to western South America.<ref name="POWO-1"/> It was first described by [[Michel Adanson]] in 1763.<ref name="IPNI"/> The genus is named for Greek poet [[Nicander]] of [[Colophon (city)|Colophon]], who wrote about plants<ref name="Nee-1993"/> – notably in his poem ''Alexipharmaca'', which treats of poisons and their antidotes.

{{As of|2019|March}}, [[Plants of the World Online]] accepted three species:<ref name="POWO-1"/>
*''[[Nicandra john-tyleriana]]'' <small>S.Leiva & Pereyra</small>
*''[[Nicandra physalodes]]'' <small>(L.) Gaertn.</small>
*''[[Nicandra yacheriana]]'' <small>S.Leiva</small>

From 1763 until 2007, when ''Nicandra john-tyleriana'' was described,<ref name="POWO-2"/> the only species in the genus was ''Nicandra physalodes''. A third species, ''Nicandra yacheriana'', was described in 2010.<ref name="POWO-3"/>
